passages.p1: Read the email from Nina to her dad. Choose the correct word for each gap. The first one is done for you. Dear Dad, On Sunday I went for a long bike [[1]]. First I checked the air in my [[2]]. I rode along a quiet country [[3]]. I always wear a helmet on my [[4]]. The wind felt cool on my [[5]]. I came home feeling happy but very [[6]].
passages.p2: Put the sentences in the correct order. The first sentence is fixed.
passages.p3:
A. In little more than a decade, social media has woven itself into the fabric of everyday life. Billions of people now scroll through feeds, share photos and exchange messages on platforms that barely existed a generation ago. This technology has changed how we work, shop, learn and relate to one another. Few inventions have spread so far and so fast.

B. Many of its effects are genuinely positive and easy to celebrate. Social media lets friends and families stay close across great distances and helps people find others who share their interests. It can spread useful information quickly and give a voice to those who were once ignored. In times of crisis, it can coordinate help with astonishing speed.

C. Alongside these benefits, however, lie real concerns about mental health. A steady diet of carefully edited images can leave users feeling that everyone else's life is better than their own. Studies have linked heavy use to higher rates of anxiety and low self-esteem, especially among the young. The endless comparison can quietly erode contentment.

D. The way these platforms are designed deserves close attention. Features such as endless scrolling and constant notifications are engineered to capture and hold our attention for as long as possible. The longer we stay, the more advertisements we see, which is how the companies make their money. Our time, in effect, has become the product being sold.

E. Social media has also transformed the way information travels through society. News now spreads faster than ever, but so do rumours, half-truths and outright lies. Because shocking content tends to attract the most clicks, false stories can outrun careful corrections. Sorting reliable facts from convincing fiction has become a vital modern skill.

F. The technology raises difficult questions about privacy as well. Every like, search and pause is recorded and analysed to build detailed pictures of who we are. This data can be used to target us with adverts or, more worryingly, to influence our opinions. Many users remain unaware of just how much they reveal.

G. None of this means social media is simply good or bad. Like any powerful tool, its effects depend heavily on how it is designed and how we choose to use it. With greater awareness and a little self-discipline, individuals can enjoy the benefits while limiting the harm. The challenge for society is to shape the technology before it shapes us.

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

If the negotiations break down tomorrow, the union _____ industrial action immediately.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. Nhận diện dấu hiệu ngữ pháp: câu điều kiện loại 1.
2. Quy tắc: dùng "will" cho hành động trong tương lai.
3. Đáp án: {will take} — dùng "will" cho hành động tương lai trong câu điều kiện.
[/tuduy]
[td]Nếu các cuộc đàm phán thất bại vào ngày mai, công đoàn sẽ tiến hành hành động công nghiệp ngay lập tức.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

She _____ living here since she was a child.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. "since she was a child" → kéo dài từ quá khứ đến nay
2. Hiện tại hoàn thành tiếp diễn: has/have been + V-ing
3. Đáp án: {has been} — present perfect continuous
[/tuduy]
[td]Cô ấy đã sống ở đây từ khi còn nhỏ.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

Neither _____ I.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. Ngữ cảnh: đáp lại câu phủ định với "can't" → dùng cùng trợ động từ
2. Cấu trúc: Neither + trợ động từ + S (đồng tình phủ định)
3. Đáp án: {can} — Neither can I
[/tuduy]
[td]Tôi cũng không (thể).[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

The letter _____ written in French.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. Câu bị động: S + be + V3 (written)
2. Ngữ cảnh quá khứ → "was" + written
3. Đáp án: {was} — bị động quá khứ đơn
[/tuduy]
[td]Bức thư được viết bằng tiếng Pháp.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

He told me that he _____ tired.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. "told" = quá khứ → câu gián tiếp lùi thì
2. is → was (lùi thì)
3. Đáp án: {was} — reported speech
[/tuduy]
[td]Anh ấy nói với tôi rằng anh ấy mệt.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

She asked me where I _____.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. "asked" = quá khứ → câu hỏi gián tiếp lùi thì
2. "Where do you live?" → "where I lived"
3. Đáp án: {lived} — reported question
[/tuduy]
[td]Cô ấy hỏi tôi sống ở đâu.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

If you _____ to assemble the unit yourself, please ensure all screws are tightened before use.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. Nhận diện dấu hiệu ngữ pháp: câu điều kiện loại 1 sử dụng hiện tại.
2. Quy tắc: "If" + hiện tại tiếp diễn cho hành động tương lai.
3. Đáp án: {are intending} — sử dụng hiện tại tiếp diễn cho tương lai.
[/tuduy]
[td]Nếu bạn "đang có ý định" lắp ráp đơn vị đó một mình, hãy đảm bảo tất cả các ốc vít được siết chặt trước khi sử dụng.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

I don't have _____ money left.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. "money" là danh từ không đếm được
2. Danh từ không đếm được → dùng "much" (không dùng "many")
3. Đáp án: {much} — much + uncountable noun
[/tuduy]
[td]Tôi không còn nhiều tiền.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

If water _____ to 100 degrees Celsius at sea level, it boils.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. Câu có "If" cho thấy đây là câu điều kiện.
2. Câu điều kiện loại 0 dùng thì hiện tại đơn cho cả mệnh đề.
3. Đáp án: {is heated} — Câu điều kiện loại 0 diễn tả sự thật hiển nhiên.
[/tuduy]
[td]Nếu nước "được đun nóng" đến 100 độ C ở mức độ biển, nó sẽ sôi.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

She _____ reading when the phone rang.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. "rang" = quá khứ đơn → hành động đang diễn ra tại thời điểm đó
2. Quá khứ tiếp diễn: was/were + V-ing
3. Đáp án: {was} — past continuous
[/tuduy]
[td]Cô ấy đang đọc sách khi điện thoại reo.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

He is _____ tallest boy in the class.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. So sánh nhất (tallest) → luôn đi kèm mạo từ "the"
2. Quy tắc: the + adj-est / the most + adj
3. Đáp án: {the} — the + superlative
[/tuduy]
[td]Anh ấy là cậu bé cao nhất lớp.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

I need _____ information about the course.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. "information" là danh từ không đếm được → không dùng "a" hay "many"
2. Dùng "some" với danh từ không đếm được trong câu khẳng định
3. Đáp án: {some} — some + uncountable
[/tuduy]
[td]Tôi cần một số thông tin về khóa học.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

She has _____ to Paris three times.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. "has been to" = đã từng đến (và đã về); "has gone to" = đã đi (chưa về)
2. Ba lần → đã từng đến và trở về → "been"
3. Đáp án: {been} — has been to (kinh nghiệm)
[/tuduy]
[td]Cô ấy đã đến Paris ba lần rồi.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

The teacher _____ us to study hard for the test.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. Sau "said" không có tân ngữ trực tiếp; sau "told" CÓ tân ngữ (us)
2. tell + someone + to V = bảo ai làm gì
3. Đáp án: {told} — told us to…
[/tuduy]
[td]Cô giáo bảo chúng tôi học chăm cho bài kiểm tra.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

She _____ that we should leave early.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. Cấu trúc: suggest + (that) + S + should + V
2. "told" cần tân ngữ trực tiếp; "said me" sai ngữ pháp
3. Đáp án: {suggested} — suggest + that-clause
[/tuduy]
[td]Cô ấy gợi ý rằng chúng ta nên đi sớm.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

He _____ to lend me his bicycle.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. offer + to V = đề nghị làm gì cho ai
2. "said" không dùng + to V; "suggested" + V-ing
3. Đáp án: {offered} — offered to lend
[/tuduy]
[td]Anh ấy đề nghị cho tôi mượn xe đạp.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

She _____ me not to tell anyone.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. ask + someone + (not) to V = yêu cầu/nhờ ai (không) làm gì
2. "said" không dùng + me + to V; "suggested" + V-ing
3. Đáp án: {asked} — asked me not to…
[/tuduy]
[td]Cô ấy nhờ tôi đừng nói với ai.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

He _____ to help me move house.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. promise + to V = hứa sẽ làm gì
2. "said" không dùng + to V trực tiếp; "told" cần tân ngữ
3. Đáp án: {promised} — promised to help
[/tuduy]
[td]Anh ấy hứa sẽ giúp tôi chuyển nhà.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

They _____ to come to the party.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. refuse + to V = từ chối làm gì
2. "deny" + V-ing (phủ nhận); "reject" + danh từ (bác bỏ)
3. Đáp án: {refused} — refused to come
[/tuduy]
[td]Họ từ chối đến dự tiệc.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

She _____ me to bring an umbrella.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. remind + someone + to V = nhắc ai làm gì
2. "said" không + me + to V; "suggested" + V-ing
3. Đáp án: {reminded} — reminded me to…
[/tuduy]
[td]Cô ấy nhắc tôi mang theo ô.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

He _____ for being late to the meeting.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. apologise + for + V-ing = xin lỗi vì đã làm gì
2. "sorry" là tính từ (không phải động từ); "excused" không + for V-ing
3. Đáp án: {apologised} — apologised for…
[/tuduy]
[td]Anh ấy xin lỗi vì đến muộn cuộc họp.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

You _____ smoke in the hospital.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. Bệnh viện → quy định CẤM hút thuốc
2. "mustn't" = cấm; "don't have to" = không cần; "needn't" = không cần
3. Đáp án: {mustn't} — cấm đoán
[/tuduy]
[td]Bạn không được hút thuốc trong bệnh viện.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

She _____ me to her birthday party.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. invite + someone + to + sự kiện = mời ai đến
2. "suggested" + V-ing; "offered" + to V (đề nghị giúp)
3. Đáp án: {invited} — invited me to…
[/tuduy]
[td]Cô ấy mời tôi đến bữa tiệc sinh nhật.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

I'll call you when I _____ home.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. Sau "when" (mệnh đề thời gian chỉ tương lai) → dùng thì hiện tại đơn
2. Không dùng "will" trong mệnh đề when chỉ tương lai
3. Đáp án: {get} — present simple after "when"
[/tuduy]
[td]Mình sẽ gọi cho bạn khi mình về nhà.[/td]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

He asked me what I _____ doing.
questions.explanation:
[tuduy]
1. "asked" = quá khứ → câu gián tiếp lùi thì
2. Hiện tại tiếp diễn → quá khứ tiếp diễn: am doing → was doing
3. Đáp án: {was} — lùi thì trong câu gián tiếp
[/tuduy]
[td]Anh ấy hỏi tôi đang làm gì.[/td]

questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I remember quite a lot from school. I really enjoyed our biology lessons, especially studying plants and animals. Our teacher once helped us grow beans in jars, which made the whole topic feel exciting and real.

questions.content:
Writing — Part 3 - Three responses

Anika: Who is your favourite inventor or scientist, and why?
questions.sampleAnswer: My favourite scientist is Marie Curie. I admire her because she worked extremely hard and discovered new elements. She also proved that women can succeed in science, which I find very inspiring and encouraging for everyone today.

questions.content:
Writing — Part 4 - Informal and formal emails

Write an email to your friend. Write about your feelings and what ideas you have. Write about 50 words. Recommended time: 10 minutes.
questions.sampleAnswer:
Hi Kai!
Our science group is putting together an exhibition next month and they want it to work for all ages! I think they should have volcano experiments and a stargazing corner for kids, plus a robotics demo for the adults. I reckon it should be free — charging would put families off.
Sounds fun, right?
Daisy

questions.content:
Writing — Part 4 - Informal and formal emails

Write an email to the planning team. Write about your ideas for the exhibition and whether you think there should be an entry fee. Write 120–150 words. Recommended time: 20 minutes.
questions.sampleAnswer:
Dear Planning Team,
I am writing to share my ideas for the upcoming science exhibition. I am very excited about the event and believe it has great potential to inspire visitors of all ages.
For younger visitors, I suggest interactive stations such as a baking-soda volcano experiment, a magnetic maze, and a stargazing corner with a small telescope. These hands-on activities would capture children's curiosity and make learning enjoyable.
For older visitors, I recommend a robotics demonstration, a short talk on recent scientific breakthroughs, and a display showcasing local inventors. These elements would provide intellectual stimulation for adults and elderly attendees alike.
Regarding the entry fee, I believe the event should remain free of charge. Making it accessible to everyone would maximise attendance, especially for families. If additional funding is needed, a donation box at the exit would be a fair compromise.
I hope these suggestions are helpful.
Yours sincerely,
Adam Fletcher

  2. To do this, they use the light that comes from the sun each day.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 1 - Personal information

Tell me about your family.
questions.sampleAnswer: My family has four people — my parents, my sister, and me. My father works at a bank. My mother is a teacher. We live together in a small house. I love my family very much.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 1 - Personal information

What are the benefits of cooking?
questions.sampleAnswer: Cooking has many benefits. First, you can save money because eating at home is cheaper than eating out. The food is also healthier because you know what ingredients you use. Cooking is also a fun activity.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 1 - Personal information

How do you usually get to work or school?
questions.sampleAnswer: I usually go to school by bus. The bus stop is near my house. It takes about thirty minutes. Sometimes when the weather is nice, I ride my bicycle. I like cycling because it is good exercise.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 2 - Describe a picture

Describe the picture.
questions.sampleAnswer: I see a group of people watching a street performer. A young man is playing the guitar. The people around him are smiling and enjoying the music. One person is sitting in a wheelchair. Everyone looks happy.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 2 - Describe a picture

Do you enjoy watching street performances? Why?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I enjoy watching street performances. The music is free and fun. It makes me feel happy when I walk in the city. Street performers are very talented. I always stop to watch them.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 2 - Describe a picture

Why are street performances important in a city?
questions.sampleAnswer: Street performances are important because they make the city lively and fun. They bring people together. They also help artists show their talent and earn money. Street art makes a city more beautiful and interesting.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 3 - Compare two pictures

Describe the two pictures.
questions.sampleAnswer: In the first picture, I see people learning at a museum. They are looking at old objects and paintings. A guide is explaining something. It looks interesting. In the second picture, I see people learning in a library. They are sitting at desks reading books. It is very quiet. There are many bookshelves.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 3 - Compare two pictures

What do you think of learning in a museum and in a library?
questions.sampleAnswer: At a museum, you can see real things and learn in a fun way. It is more interesting than books. But you cannot study deeply. In a library, you can read many books and study quietly. But it can be boring.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 3 - Compare two pictures

What do you think about learning history? Why?
questions.sampleAnswer: I think learning history is important. History teaches us about the past. We can learn from old mistakes. It helps us understand our country and culture. But sometimes history lessons are boring if they only use books.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 4 - Discuss an abstract topic

Tell me about a time when you attended a sports event.
questions.sampleAnswer:
Last year, I went to watch a football match with my friends. It was between two famous teams. The stadium was very big and full of people. It was a very exciting day.
The atmosphere was amazing. Everyone was shouting and cheering for their team. People wore the team colours and waved flags. When our team scored a goal, everyone jumped and shouted with joy. I felt very excited.
I think people enjoy watching sports because it is exciting. You don't know who will win. Watching sports with other fans is fun. It also brings people together. Sports give us strong emotions and good memories.
